original_value: Efficiently rendering direct lighting from millions of dynamic light sources using Monte Carlo integration remains a challenging problem, even for off-line rendering systems. We introduce a new algorithm---ReSTIR---that renders such lighting interactively, at high quality, and without needing to maintain complex data structures. We repeatedly resample a set of candidate light samples and apply further spatial and temporal resampling to leverage information from relevant nearby samples. We derive an unbiased Monte Carlo estimator for this approach, and show that it achieves equal-error 6×-60× faster than state-of-the-art methods. A biased estimator reduces noise further and is 35×-65× faster, at the cost of some energy loss. We implemented our approach on the GPU, rendering complex scenes containing up to 3.4 million dynamic, emissive triangles in under 50 ms per frame while tracing at most 8 rays per pixel.

result.paraphrase: Direct lighting from millions of dynamic light sources is still difficult to render efficiently with Monte Carlo integration, even in offline renderers. We present ReSTIR, a new algorithm that produces this lighting interactively and at high quality without requiring complex data structures. It works by repeatedly resampling candidate light samples, then using additional spatial and temporal resampling to exploit nearby relevant samples. We derive an unbiased Monte Carlo estimator for the method and show that it reaches the same error 6×–60× faster than state-of-the-art approaches. A biased estimator cuts noise even more and is 35×–65× faster, but with some energy loss. Our GPU implementation renders complex scenes with up to 3.4 million dynamic emissive triangles in under 50 ms per frame while tracing at most 8 rays per pixel.
